claims.text: Adding 5-10 wt% excess Zr powder will act as an in-situ oxygen getter.
Zr will scavenge oxygen associated with hydride decomposition and ambient leaks.
Oxygen scavenging by Zr will prevent nucleation of alpha-HCP phases.
The hydrides TaH0.5, NbH, HfH2, TiH2, and ZrH2 will decompose sequentially at characteristic temperatures.
The order of hydride decomposition is governed by hydride formation enthalpies.
An argon atmosphere with oxygen partial pressure below 1 ppm is suitable for the proposed process.
A quenching rate above 100 K/s will retain the high-temperature beta-BCC phase.
Getter activity will form a stable Zr-O solid solution or ZrO2 precipitates.
Formation of Zr-O species will sequester oxygen and prevent its dissolution into the HfNbTaTiZr matrix.
Zr has sufficiently high oxygen affinity to oxidize preferentially relative to the other alloy constituents.
ZrO2 has a lower formation enthalpy than the other relevant oxides in the system.
Preferential oxidation of Zr will keep matrix oxygen activity below the threshold for alpha-HCP stabilization.
Rapidly quenched material containing the Zr getter will have a metastable single-phase beta-BCC structure.
The processed alloy will reach greater than 98% density.
The rapidly quenched alloy will have a grain size of 10-50 micrometers.
No detectable alpha-HCP or alpha-Ti phase will remain after rapid quenching.
A control processed without Zr getter will form significant alpha-HCP phase.
The control without Zr getter will have reduced density because of oxygen-induced phase segregation and porosity.
Excessive Zr getter can alter the equiatomic alloy stoichiometry or produce brittle oxide inclusions.
BCC lattice-parameter shifts can be used to infer oxygen content in this experiment.

contradictions.description: The intervention adds 5-10 wt% excess Zr, while the outcome calls the final alloy equiatomic and the boundary requires that stoichiometry not be altered significantly. No removal route or quantitative oxygen inventory is provided to show that the added Zr is fully consumed or excluded from the alloy matrix.

The mediator permits formation of ZrO2 precipitates, whereas the outcome describes a homogeneous single-phase beta-BCC material. Retained crystalline ZrO2 precipitates would make the overall material multiphase unless 'single-phase' is explicitly restricted to the metallic matrix.
